summary.goal: Implement the tier-based execution coordinator that advances a build through its tiers, creating and monitoring Forge runs, handling failures, and supporting pause/resume/cancel at the build level.

acceptance_criteria.description: startBuild() begins execution: fetches tier 0 plans from Planner, creates runs, transitions build to 'running'
Each plan is fetched via PlannerClient.fetchPlanVersion() and transformed via transformToForgePlan() before run creation
Within a tier, up to concurrency_limit runs execute in parallel
When all runs in a tier complete successfully, the coordinator advances to the next tier
When a run fails in tier N: dependent tiers are blocked, sibling runs in tier N continue, build status becomes 'failed' once tier settles
When skip_completed=true, plans with a recent successful run are marked as 'skipped' in build_runs and not re-executed
pauseBuild() pauses all in-progress runs and stops scheduling new ones
resumeBuild() resumes paused runs and continues tier progression
cancelBuild() cancels all in-progress and pending runs
Build completes when all tiers are done (or when blocked by failure with no more actionable tiers)
Coordinator survives server restart: on startup, resumes any builds in 'running' state
Works with both test mode and real mode — mode is passed to each run

observations: The coordinator monitors runs by polling (like the existing orchestrator monitors tasks)
Run completion detection: poll build_runs statuses, compare against expected counts per tier
The coordinator does NOT use sub_plan_id — it creates independent top-level runs
Each run goes through the normal Forge execution pipeline (orchestrator or test executor)
The coordinator is a service instantiated in createForgeService(), similar to how the orchestrator is created
Server restart recovery: query for builds with status='running', resume monitoring

architect.execution_loop: 1. Start tier 0 → create runs (up to concurrency limit) → 2. Monitor runs (poll interval) → 3. Run completes: update build_run status → 4. All tier N runs done? → advance to tier N+1 → repeat → 5. All tiers done? → finalize build
architect.failure_model: Run failure in tier N → mark build_run as failed → continue sibling runs → when tier settles: if any failed, block higher tiers, set build status to 'failed'. User can retry failed tier or cancel.
architect.concurrency: Per-build concurrency_limit (default 5). Within a tier, schedule up to limit runs. As runs complete, schedule more from the same tier if available.

steps.title: Implement BuildCoordinator class with config and state tracking
steps.description: Create the BuildCoordinator class with constructor accepting config (storage, plannerClient, scheduleReadyTasks, forgeConfig), internal state maps for tracking active builds, and the public API surface.

acceptance_criteria.description: BuildCoordinatorConfig interface: { storage: ForgeStorage, plannerClient: PlannerClient, scheduleReadyTasks: (runId: string) => void, forgeConfig: ForgeConfig, pollIntervalMs?: number (default 3000) }
BuildCoordinator extends EventEmitter. Private state: activeBuildLoops Map<buildId, boolean>, storage, plannerClient, scheduleReadyTasks, forgeConfig, pollIntervalMs
Public methods declared: startBuild(buildId), pauseBuild(buildId), resumeBuild(buildId), cancelBuild(buildId), recoverActiveBuilds(), shutdown()

Typed event emission: this.emit(eventType, { buildId, data }) for build lifecycle events. Event types: build_started, tier_started, run_started, run_completed, run_failed, tier_completed, build_completed, build_failed, build_paused, build_cancelled
subscribeToBuild(buildId, listener) and unsubscribeFromBuild(buildId, listener) convenience methods that filter events by buildId

architecture.pattern: Class-based service extending EventEmitter (from 'events'). Config injection via constructor. State tracking with Maps. Async execution loops. Emits typed events for SSE consumption.

steps.title: Implement startBuild() with tier 0 execution
steps.description: Implement startBuild that transitions build to 'running', resolves tier 0 plans, creates runs and build_runs, schedules execution, and starts the monitoring loop.

acceptance_criteria.description: Transitions build status from 'pending' to 'running'
Reads tier 0 plan_ids from build.tiers
For each plan_id: fetches plan via plannerClient.fetchPlanVersion(planId), transforms via transformToForgePlan(planVersion, forgeConfig)
If skip_completed=true and getRecentSuccessfulRun(planId) returns a run, marks build_run as 'skipped' instead of creating a new run
Creates Run via createRun(forgePlan), saves to storage, creates BuildRun linking build_id→run_id
Calls scheduleReadyTasks(runId) for each created run (respecting concurrency_limit)
Kicks off the async monitorBuildLoop(buildId)

architecture.concurrency_model: Track in-flight run count. Schedule up to concurrency_limit runs. When a run completes in the monitor loop, schedule next available run from same tier.
architecture.error_handling: If plannerClient.fetchPlanVersion fails for a plan, mark that build_run as 'failed' with error, continue with remaining plans in tier.

steps.title: Implement monitorBuildLoop() for tier progression
steps.description: Implement the async polling loop that monitors run completions, advances tiers, and finalizes the build.

acceptance_criteria.description: Polls every pollIntervalMs while activeBuildLoops.get(buildId) is true
For current tier: reads all build_runs, checks each run's status from storage.getRun(runId), syncs build_run status
When a run completes: updates build_run to 'completed', if under concurrency_limit schedules next unstarted run in same tier
When a run fails: updates build_run to 'failed'

When all build_runs in tier are terminal (completed/failed/skipped): if all succeeded/skipped, emit 'tier_completed' event, start next tier via startTier(buildId, tierNum+1). If any failed, emit 'build_failed' event, set build status to 'failed' and stop.
When all tiers done: set build status to 'completed', set completed_at, emit 'build_completed' event
Stall detection: if no progress for 100 iterations, log warning
Emit events at each state change: 'run_started' when scheduling, 'run_completed'/'run_failed' on status sync, 'tier_started' when advancing tiers

architecture.pattern: Same while(true) + delay pattern as orchestrator.executeRun(). Check activeBuildLoops map for early exit on pause/cancel.
architecture.tier_advancement: startTier() is reusable — same logic as the tier 0 path in startBuild but for tier N. Extract shared helper: executeTier(buildId, tierNum).

steps.title: Implement pause, resume, cancel build operations
steps.description: Implement the three control operations that modify build state and propagate to child runs.

acceptance_criteria.description: pauseBuild(): sets activeBuildLoops.set(buildId, false) to stop monitoring, pauses all running runs via storage.updateRunStatus(runId, 'paused'), updates build status to 'paused', emits 'build_paused' event
resumeBuild(): transitions build back to 'running', resumes paused runs, restarts monitorBuildLoop(), emits 'build_started' event (resume)

cancelBuild(): stops monitoring loop, cancels all non-terminal runs via storage.updateRunStatus(runId, 'cancelled'), sets all pending build_runs to 'failed', updates build status to 'cancelled', emits 'build_cancelled' event
All three validate state transitions before acting (e.g., can't pause a completed build)

architecture.pattern: Each operation: validate transition → update build status → propagate to child runs → manage monitoring loop

steps.title: Implement server restart recovery
steps.description: Add recoverActiveBuilds() that finds builds in 'running' state on startup and resumes their monitoring loops.

acceptance_criteria.description: recoverActiveBuilds(): queries listBuilds({ status: 'running' }), for each starts monitorBuildLoop(buildId)
Monitor loop picks up where it left off — reads current tier state from build_runs, continues from first incomplete tier
Logs recovery actions: '[BuildCoordinator] Recovering N active builds'

architecture.invocation: Called from createForgeService() after storage initialization, before router creation

steps.title: Wire BuildCoordinator into createForgeService()
steps.description: Instantiate BuildCoordinator in createForgeService() and expose it for the build API handlers. Add shutdown hook.

acceptance_criteria.description: BuildCoordinator instantiated with { storage, plannerClient, scheduleReadyTasks, forgeConfig } in createForgeService()
recoverActiveBuilds() called during initialization
coordinator.shutdown() called in service shutdown hook
BuildCoordinator passed to createForgeRouter() via ForgeRouterDeps

Created in both real and test mode — plannerClient is always created (it fetches plans to create runs regardless of execution mode). In test mode, scheduleReadyTasks comes from testExecutor; in real mode from orchestrator.

architecture.pattern: Same wiring pattern as existing orchestrator — created in factory, passed to router via deps
